description: Lists a Reddit user's recent comments. Returns comments with body, score, subreddit, parent link, and timestamp plus an `after` cursor. Example: name='spez' sort='top'.

after.description: Opaque pagination cursor: the previous response's `after` value, exactly as it was returned. The format is not stable, and a hand-written Reddit fullname loses the paging depth the cursor carries. Absent on the opening page. A null `after` on a response means there is no next page; it does not by itself mean the listing is complete, because Reddit often stops serving a busy listing long before it runs out. That final response carries `listing_status`: `complete`, `truncated` or `unknown`, and only `complete` means nothing is missing.

include_parents.description: true also fills `parent_id` on the first 10 comments when the page is served from the profile page (which does not carry it), one extra read per comment inside the call's own time budget, so the call answers slower; a comment whose read fails keeps parent_id null, and `meta.parents_filled` says how many were filled. false or omitted (default) returns the page as served.

limit.description: Maximum items returned, 1 to 100. The API clamps out-of-range values; the endpoint default applies when omitted.

name.description: Reddit username WITHOUT the u/ prefix (e.g. 'spez'). Required (path parameter). Required: send `name` or its alias `username`.

sort.description: Sort order for a user's comments. 'new' = most recent (default), 'hot', 'top' (in the `t` window), 'controversial'.

username.description: Alias of `name`; send one of them. `name` is the canonical name.

name: reddit_user_comments
title: List User Comments
